clue.text: He coaxes reluctant dancer to writhe about with her holding arm

parts.note: to snake is to twist and writhe
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: holding says the word her wraps around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer is urged to twist about while her arm is held.
explanation.walkthrough: The dancer is the snake, reluctant because it must be coaxed out of its basket by the music; 'writhe' is a verb, as a snake moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer with a pipe entices a cobra to sway and rise from its basket, a dancer that never volunteers.

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters that follow are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer who feints and throws a right punch on shaky legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' shuffles FEINTS with R. 'Slug' reads as a punch, continuing the boxing picture, but it is a slug of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a quick swig of spirits, and a snifter is a small measure of the same.

clue.text: Temperature on high following air-conditioning malfunction

indicators.note: following says the next pieces come after the air-conditioning letters

parts.note: up means high, raised

explanation.surface: After the air-conditioning breaks down the temperature soars.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts T above UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is playing up or acting up is failing to work properly, the idiom for misbehaving.

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A European Union ally arranges the movement of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like freight but is the verb meaning to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with joy, the same as delighting them utterly.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tough guy swinging an axe is a bit of an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' is a verb here, to trick, not the idiot the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to trick or deceive them, as a practical deception does.

indicators.note: a rebellious group breaks ranks, so the remaining letters are put out of order
lacking says a letter is taken away from the word chorister

explanation.surface: An unruly choirboy without any particular gift for speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes S from CHORISTER, leaving CHORITER, and 'Rebellious' shuffles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, so it stands for eloquence or fine language.

clue.text: Compere, familiarly, seems clever off and on

indicators.note: off and on means every other letter is used, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A host who comes across as bright only some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: From SEEMSCLEVER take the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial word, from the initials MC, means a master of ceremonies or show host.

clue.text: The mob he organised is something enormous

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd marshalled by one man becomes a huge force.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a biblical beast, now any huge creature or thing.

clue.text: Modest husband belonging to exclusive social class

indicators.note: belonging to says the husband letter sits inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a closed hereditary social class

explanation.surface: A demure husband from a closed social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in conduct, a sense of modest.

parts.note: to inter is to bury
face means one's features

explanation.surface: The faces of the people of a northern English town have something in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town near Manchester, which tempts a geographical reading; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An interface is a common boundary or connection where two systems meet.

indicators.note: being talked about says the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to check is to bar or stop

explanation.surface: A pub with an arty clientele is the talk of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' tempts as arty, but it is someone from Bohemia, now part of the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historic region of the Czech Republic, so a native is Czech.

parts.note: taken as written
pups are young upstarts, and also young animals

explanation.surface: Microcredit offered to the young.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional small amounts added to a loan or a phone balance are top-ups.

indicators.note: loses says letters are dropped from the beauty word

parts.note: loveliness means beauty
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A jilted beauty loses her composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like composure, but it is IN, fashionable, taken out of LOVELINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forsaken has been abandoned and so is without affection.

clue.text: US raid 'compromised' — that's the line coming from centre

indicators.note: compromised means damaged or put at risk, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An American military raid has been compromised.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a radius is a straight line from a circle's middle to its edge.

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: The ocean is essentially melancholy.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep down is an idiom meaning at heart or fundamentally.

clue.text: Refute Sun's in favour of stopping deception in football

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the next letters fill the deception word

parts.note: a dive is a feigned fall to win a foul
S is the abbreviation for sun
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A tabloid backs a crackdown on players feigning fouls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which suits the surface; here it is only S.
explanation.definitionFit: To disprove a claim is to show it false, which is to refute it.

indicators.note: a version is a variant form, so the letters appear rearranged

explanation.surface: A board game sold in a budget edition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Indian-derived race game played with dice and counters on a cross-shaped board.

definitions.meaning: lethargic means without energy or enthusiasm
read literally, having no list of items

explanation.surface: A sluggish meeting with nothing scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: Without energy, or punningly without a list, the word covers both senses.

parts.note: a stammered F followed by Rene, a common French man's name
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A Frenchman stammers, a nervous habit when he is overwrought.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'F-' supplies its own letter, F, before RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic and wildly agitated, close to hysterical.

indicators.note: accommodates means holds within, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: a font is a typeface

explanation.surface: An e-reader's typeface handles medieval texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like the e-reader brand, but it is the verb, to stir up.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to stir it up or inflame it, as kindling starts a fire.

clue.text: With 40% cutback analyst is one with target to hit

indicators.note: cutback with the 40% before it says four of the ten letters are cut away from the front, leaving the back part

parts.note: a researcher is an analyst

explanation.surface: An analyst facing budget cuts still has targets to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With 40%' sizes the cut: RESEARCHER has ten letters, so 'cutback' removes the first four, RESE. 'Target' is literal, an archer's target.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows at a target, so is literally one aiming to hit it.

clue.text: Balance affected manner with righteous heart

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged
heart means the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pious person balances affectation with real virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' shuffles MANNER into REMNAN; the heart of 'righteous' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A balance is what is left over, the remainder or leftover piece.

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to mediate is to umpire, judge between parties
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A calm umpire calls out a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sedate' looks like an adjective, calm, but is the verb. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to give them calming drugs, to dose them.

indicators.note: bendy means flexible and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prepare to steady a flexible rod.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is the tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland Games.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is a long heavy wooden pole thrown in Scottish sport.

clue.text: Recommend healthy yodelling to help musical beginners when beat

indicators.note: beginners means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A tip for novices: hearty yodelling will help them keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginners' is both the surface's novices and the signal to take initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm is a regular pattern of beats in music.

clue.text: Sudden pain expelling start of gastric wind

indicators.note: expelling means forcing out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a twinge is a sudden sharp pain

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A stomach pain caused by trapped gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the verb, to wrap round, not the gas suggested by 'gastric'.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine means to twist or coil around, which is to wind.

clue.text: Gosh, Beethoven's Ninth is old-fashioned stuff

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: the ninth letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Beethoven's last symphony is dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninth' points to the Choral Symphony but means the ninth letter of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is trite or sentimental material, the source of the adjective corny.

indicators.note: backing means the hidden run is read in reverse
some says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Tribute acts for the Swedish pop group support a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince the pop star seems apt, but this is an Indian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim ruler or nobleman in India, comparable to a prince.

clue.text: Redesign a core site for specialist publications

indicators.note: redesign means rework the layout, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A website for niche titles needs a fresh layout.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure items understood only by a few, such as works for initiates.

clue.text: Impression of something about to happen here — people are gripped by it

definitions.text: Impression of something about to happen

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

indicators.note: are gripped by means are held inside

parts.note: taken as written
men means people

explanation.surface: A sense of foreboding among those present.
explanation.definitionFit: A premonition is a feeling that something is about to occur.
